title: Christopher O.H. Williams (board director, ex-Nike/adidas/Gap) ranks the Summit — 'My favorite mainstage talk was by Eric Ries'
summary: A corporate governance specialist and board director writes up his fifth Directors Summit, the one he almost skipped and calls his best yet, and singles out Eric's session from a mainstage that also held Sheila Bair and Ian Bremmer. What he takes from it is the foundation-owned and mission-locked structures, and he reads the talk as an argument for governance designed to outlast the people in the room.
blockquote: My favorite mainstage talk was by Eric Ries on his new book, "Incorruptible: Why Good Companies Go Bad... and How Great Companies Stay Great", and how foundation-owned and mission-locked companies stay true to their purpose over the long term. It was a powerful case for governance built to last.
attribution_title: Board Director · Corporate governance for retail & consumer brands · ex-Nike, adidas, Gap, VFC
